questions.question: How do I install uv on a Mac or Linux machine?
questions.answer: Run the standalone installer with curl, for example curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh, or use wget if curl is not available.

questions.question: Can I buy a paid support contract for uv with guaranteed response times?
questions.answer: I couldn't find that in the docs.

questions.question: How do I update uv to the latest version?
questions.answer: If uv was installed with the standalone installer, run uv self update; otherwise use your package manager's upgrade command, such as pip install --upgrade uv.

questions.question: How do I create a new library project that other people can install?
questions.answer: Run uv init --lib with the project name, which creates a packaged project with a src layout and a build system so it can be built and distributed.

questions.question: How do I remove a package from my dev dependencies?
questions.answer: Run uv remove with the --dev flag and the package name; the --group and --optional flags work the same way for other tables.

questions.question: When moving from pip, how do I import my requirements but keep my old pinned versions?
questions.answer: Run uv add -r requirements.in -c requirements.txt so your previously locked versions are applied as constraints and kept in the new lockfile.

questions.question: How do I make uv install every dependency group by default?
questions.answer: Set default-groups to "all" in the tool.uv section of your project settings; otherwise uv only includes the dev group by default.

questions.question: How much does uv cost for enterprise teams?
questions.answer: I couldn't find that in the docs.

questions.question: How can I check that my lock file is up to date without changing it?
questions.answer: Run uv lock --check, which reports whether the lockfile matches the project metadata and is equivalent to the --locked flag on other commands.

questions.question: How do I upgrade a locked package to a specific version?
questions.answer: Run uv lock --upgrade-package with the package name and the version, such as package==version, which changes only that package in the lockfile within the project's constraints.

questions.question: Will uv sync remove packages that are not part of my project?
questions.answer: Yes, uv sync performs exact syncing by default and removes packages that are not selected for installation; pass --inexact to keep them.

questions.question: How do I add an extra package for just one uv run command?
questions.answer: Use the --with option, for example uv run --with httpx==0.26.0, to include a dependency for that single invocation regardless of the project's requirements.

questions.question: How do I pin the Python version for my project?
questions.answer: Run uv python pin, which writes a .python-version file that uv uses as the default Python version request.

questions.question: Is there a long term support release of uv for companies that upgrade slowly?
questions.answer: I couldn't find that in the docs.

questions.question: How do I ask uv for a Python build that has no global interpreter lock?
questions.answer: Request a free-threaded variant explicitly, for example 3.13t or 3.13+freethreaded, which uv supports for CPython 3.13 and later.

questions.question: Where does uvx keep a tool's environment, and does it stick around?
questions.answer: uvx stores the tool's virtual environment in the uv cache directory and treats it as disposable, so uv cache clean deletes it and it is recreated when needed.

questions.question: How do I run a command whose package has a different name, like http from httpie?
questions.answer: Use the --from option to name the package that provides the command, for example uvx --from httpie http.

questions.question: How do I reinstall the Python versions that uv manages?
questions.answer: Run uv python install --reinstall, which reinstalls all previously installed uv-managed Python versions.

questions.question: Can uv install and manage Node JS versions as well as Python?
questions.answer: I couldn't find that in the docs.

questions.question: How do I upgrade all of my installed tools at once?
questions.answer: Run uv tool upgrade --all; upgrades respect the version constraints you gave when installing each tool.

questions.question: How do I declare dependencies inside a single Python script?
questions.answer: Use uv add --script with the script name and packages, which writes an inline metadata block listing the dependencies at the top of the script.

questions.question: Should I use a workspace if my packages have conflicting requirements?
questions.answer: No, workspaces are not suited to members with conflicting requirements; define each package as its own project and connect them with path dependencies instead.

questions.question: Can uv install a dependency straight from a Mercurial repository?

questions.question: Will uv pick up the settings I already have configured for pip?
questions.answer: No, uv does not read pip-specific configuration such as pip.conf or PIP_INDEX_URL; it uses its own variables like UV_INDEX_URL and settings in uv.toml or the tool.uv.pip table.

questions.question: Does uv have a built-in task runner for project commands, like npm scripts?
questions.answer: I couldn't find that in the docs.

questions.question: How do I create a virtual environment with uv?
questions.answer: Run uv venv, which creates a virtual environment at .venv, or pass a name or a Python version, for example uv venv --python 3.11.

questions.question: If a folder has both a uv toml file and a pyproject file, which settings does uv use?
questions.answer: uv.toml takes precedence, so uv reads configuration from it and ignores the tool.uv section of the pyproject.toml in the same directory.

questions.question: How do I clear the uv cache?
questions.answer: Run uv cache clean to remove all cache entries, or uv cache prune to remove only unused entries.

questions.question: How do I make uv put the project environment somewhere other than the default folder?
questions.answer: Set the UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT environment variable to the path you want instead of the default .venv; relative paths are resolved from the workspace root.

questions.question: How do I publish my package to PyPI with uv?
questions.answer: Run uv publish and provide a PyPI token with --token or UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN, or use trusted publishing from GitHub Actions without setting credentials.

questions.question: Can I make uv wait a week before it uses newly released packages?
questions.answer: Yes, set exclude-newer to a duration such as "1 week" to get a dependency cooldown that ignores packages newer than that duration.

questions.question: How can I make my Python app start faster inside a Docker container?
questions.answer: Compile bytecode at install time with --compile-bytecode or by setting UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1, which improves startup time at the cost of install time and image size.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to install uv in GitHub Actions?
questions.answer: Use the official astral-sh/setup-uv action, ideally pinned to a specific uv version with its version input.

questions.question: Can the uv build backend build packages with C or Rust extensions?
questions.answer: No, the uv build backend currently only supports pure Python code, so a library with extension modules needs an alternative build backend.

questions.question: How can I test my library against the oldest dependency versions it says it supports?
questions.answer: Run your tests with --resolution lowest, or --resolution lowest-direct for direct dependencies only, so uv installs the lowest compatible versions.

questions.question: Can uv produce a parts list of my app's dependencies for security auditors?
questions.answer: Yes, uv export --format cyclonedx1.5 exports the lockfile as a CycloneDX software bill of materials, which is currently a preview feature.
